instructions: The day before, or up to 2 days ahead: put 1 3/4 cups water, 3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp dark soy sauce, the 2 tea bags, the star anise, cinnamon stick, 2 bay leaves, 3/4 tsp Sichuan peppercorns, 1 1/2 tsp sugar and 3/4 tsp salt in a small pot. Bring it to a boil over medium heat, then turn it down to medium low and simmer for 10 minutes.
Take the pot off the heat and leave the marinade to cool completely. Fish out the tea bags and throw them away, but leave the spices in.

Bring a pot of water to a boil, deep enough to cover the eggs. Turn it down to low and lower the 8 eggs in gently with a ladle so they don't crack. Turn the heat back up to a gentle boil and cook them for 10 minutes for firm yolks, or 7 minutes if you like the yolks a little soft.
Meanwhile, fill a big bowl with ice and cold water. When the time is up, lift the eggs straight into it and leave them for 3 minutes.
Tap each egg all over with the back of a spoon, so the shell is cracked everywhere but still stuck to the egg. The cracks are where the marbling comes from, so be thorough but gentle.
Put the cracked eggs in a quart zip top bag and pour in the cooled marinade, spices and all. Squeeze out the air, seal it, and set it in a bowl in the fridge for 24 hours.
Peel the eggs and serve them cold or at room temperature. Keep any left over in the marinade in the fridge for up to 5 days. They get saltier and darker the longer they sit.
advance_prep_notes: Simmer the marinade, boil and crack the eggs, and leave them in the fridge for 24 hours. The day before.
method_notes: All three read versions simmer black tea with soy sauce and whole spices, boil the eggs, crack the shells all over with a spoon and steep them so the marinade seeps into the cracks. Omnivore's Cookbook uses light and dark soy, star anise, cinnamon, bay leaves, Sichuan peppercorns, sugar and salt, cools the marinade first and steeps the eggs in the fridge for 24 hours. Onolicious Hawaii uses a similar cooled marinade with cloves in place of the peppercorns and steeps for 24 to 48 hours, and Karen's Kitchen Stories steams the eggs, adds five spice and orange zest, and simmers the cracked eggs in the tea before leaving them overnight. This one follows Omnivore's Cookbook, sized to 8 eggs. Onolicious Hawaii shows 5 stars from 77 reviews but no rating count, so it isn't counted for the lead.
